routine.prologue: endbr64, push rbx only, no stack reserve, no canary check

arguments.rdi: hidden return-value slot (basic_string object to construct)
arguments.rsi: lhs string object (pointer at +0x00, size at +0x08, SSO buffer or capacity at +0x10)

routine.result: rax = rdi on return; the return slot holds lhs bytes followed by rhs bytes

path_choice.total: lhs size + rhs size, computed as rhs size + lhs size
insert_condition_notes: capacity(lhs) is 15 when lhs is SSO, else lhs capacity at +0x10; same rule for rhs
an SSO lhs with total <= 15 takes the append path (capacity test passes first)
an SSO lhs with total > 15 and an SSO rhs takes the append path (rhs capacity 15 < total)
an SSO lhs with total > 15 and a heap rhs takes the insert path exactly when rhs capacity >= total

length_guard.rule: if rhs size > 0x3fffffffffffffff - lhs size, throw

append_call.arguments: this = lhs, pointer = rhs data, length = rhs size

steal_into_return.heap_lhs: return pointer = lhs data, return size = lhs size, return capacity = lhs capacity; lhs reset to empty SSO (pointer = lhs + 0x10, size 0, byte 0)
steal_into_return.sso_lhs: return pointer = return + 0x10; lhs bytes plus terminating NUL copied into the return SSO buffer (copy routine at 0x5d5ac58: qword loop with 4-byte, 2-byte and 1-byte tails); return size = lhs size; lhs keeps its appended bytes

append_path.result_representation: SSO exactly when total <= 15, heap otherwise

replace_call.arguments: this = rhs, position 0, count 0, pointer = lhs data, length = lhs size
replace_call.meaning: insert the whole lhs at the front of rhs

move_construct.arguments: destination = return slot, source = replace result (rhs)
move_construct.rhs_after: moved-from; its fields are not pinned by this routine

insert_path.length_handling: no length check of its own in this routine; deferred to _M_replace, not pinned here

overload_identification.inference: libstdc++ operator+ for two string rvalues (basic_string&&, basic_string&&)
overload_identification.grounds: the routine consumes both operands (it mutates lhs on the append path and rhs on the insert path) and selects between exactly those two paths on the capacity condition; the append-only and insert-only overloads each have a single path, so the two-path shape matches only the two-rvalue overload
overload_identification.caveat: the overload name is inferred from the observed two-path structure, not from a symbol in the binary (the routine is local text; objdump labels it only by a nearby symbol offset)

consumers.argument_setup_pattern: rdi is a return slot (lea or stack-held pointer), rsi is the lhs temp, rdx is the rhs pointer (register or stack-held); at 12 of the 15 sites a move-construct call immediately precedes the argument setup, building the lhs temp
